subject.title: [Feature Request]: Session snapshots — save and load context checkpoints (/session save|load)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class named session snapshots now, and what first supported scope should land: arbitrary save/list/load, archive restore, compaction branch/restore, prompt-cache-aware fork, or a staged subset?
rationale: Current main has several adjacent primitives but no unified contract for snapshot creation, destructive restore, retention, privacy, archive import, or fork semantics, and automation should not choose those product/API boundaries.

options.title: Design core snapshot API first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the versioned contract for named checkpoints, branch/load behavior, retention, privacy, protocol, commands, CLI/UI, and tests.

options.title: Narrow to resume or archive restore
options.body: Let a smaller read-only or restore-oriented path land first while tracking named checkpoints and deterministic fork semantics separately.

options.title: Defer unified snapshots
options.body: Continue using compaction checkpoints, export commands, session switching, and partial resume work until stronger maintainer demand justifies a unified snapshot surface.

recommendation.title: Design core snapshot API first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the versioned contract for named checkpoints, branch/load behavior, retention, privacy, protocol, commands, CLI/UI, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent product-review signal on this issue and broad recent history across the session command, protocol, lifecycle, and UI surfaces.
